Main-effects design and level combinations for a cellGLoc design

Source: R/cellgloc_utils.R
dot-gloc_design_aux.Rd

What the mean step and the robust start need when a level combination has no fitted row (see .gloc_update_B).

.gloc_design_aux(
  data,
  design,
  cat_vars,
  max_patterns = .gloc_max_patterns,
  main_terms = function(vars) stats::terms(stats::reformulate(vars))
)

Arguments

data

a data.frame containing the categorical variables.

design

a one-sided formula, e.g. ~ . or ~ 1.

cat_vars

character vector naming the categorical columns.

max_patterns

enumerate every level combination up to this many, otherwise only those in the data; see .gloc_max_patterns.

main_terms

a function of the backticked variable names returning the terms of the main-effects design; an argument so the failure path can be tested.

Value

a list with U_main, the main-effects design matrix, or NULL when design has no interaction term, and patterns, or NULL when design uses no categorical variable or a variable of the model frame is not a factor. patterns is a list: id, the index of each row's level combination, where a caller marks a row whose categorical values are unknown with NA; P, the pure design row of each combination, with the columns of the design; P_main, the same for U_main (or NULL); and labels, such as "g1=c, g2=C".

Details

The main-effects design has the variables of design and none of its terms of order greater than one. The variables are read from the terms object with deparse1, so a term such as relevel(g2, ref = "B") or C(g1, contr.sum) is kept as written, and the matrix is built on the model frame that .gloc_design evaluates; the names are deparsed with backticks for reformulate(), so a factor named with a space parses. If that fails for any reason, U_main is NULL, a warning says so, and the fill uses the weighted mean only. (Corrected: the first 7.4.1 fix rebuilt the formula from backticked model-frame names, and a function call in an interaction term made imputeCellGLoc stop with "object not found".)

The level combinations are all combinations of the levels of the design's variables when there are at most .gloc_max_patterns of them, and otherwise those that occur in the data.
